en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Training Rule on Defecating on Green Grass.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks voided excrement, urine, and spittle upon green vegetation...
[as before] ... "The training is to be observed: 'When not ill, I shall not void excrement, urine, or spittle upon green vegetation.
One who is not ill must not void excrement, urine, or spittle upon green vegetation.
Whoever, out of disrespect, while not being ill, voids excrement, urine, or spittle on green vegetation, commits an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
There is no offense if it is unintentional.
In the case of one who is lacking mindfulness, one who is unaware, or one who is ill.
When made on non-green ground, it covers over green ground;
"For one who is a first offender.
The fourteenth training rule is concluded.
